reason: The prepared tank can now receive the water needed to store heat.

effect: The tank now contains water around the separate coolant coil and is ready for a heat source.
reaction: The separate fluid paths make the setup understandable.
reason: The indoor heat-recovery connection should supply process warmth to the tank's coil.
expectation: The coil will connect to the recovery loop and warm the tank water.

effect: The coil is connected to the process cooling loop, and the warm water tank completes the heat-storage goal.
reaction: The thermostat and separate fluid paths made the finished system feel physically understandable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the tank to heat recovery was the most worthwhile step: it brought the assembly together and explained how process warmth can be stored and released into the room.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to fill the tank twice before insulation was installed felt repetitive; neither rejection explained what preparation was missing.

surprise.text: Inspecting the steel automatically built the tank, and filling it was unavailable until the coil and insulation were installed.

arbitrary.text: Requiring insulation before adding water felt like a game-imposed ordering constraint rather than an obvious physical necessity, although insulation itself has a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue: the heat-recovery assembly offered a satisfying, practical explanation of how the station reuses energy, despite the frustrating ordering constraint.
